idiom_name: Mongoose embedded subdocuments saved with the parent document
implementation_notes: Node's document-store idiom is the most literal modern realization: a Mongoose schema nests child schemas as subdocument arrays or single nested paths, and the framework's documentation states that subdocuments are not saved individually - they are saved whenever their top-level parent document is saved. That is the composite entity with the store performing the unit of work: mutate the parent, call parent.save() once, and dependents are validated and written with it. On the relational side Sequelize plays the same role with hasMany/belongsTo plus onDelete/onUpdate options, but cascading saves there are explicit rather than automatic, and Mongoose's 16 MB document limit bounds how large a cluster may grow.
pitfalls: Subdocuments have no independent identity: cross-parent queries are awkward and the whole cluster travels on every read.
A document has a hard size ceiling (16 MB in MongoDB): a growing cluster eventually fails writes instead of degrading gradually.
Calling save() on a subdocument is a no-op that still runs middleware, so 'I saved the child' bugs are invisible.
